Maybe I'm not in the right head space, but my first thought was "but how much water does this thing need? What if it rains?" I know that isn't really necessary for the story, but it would add a little bit more "science" to the concept.

My idea of an origin story: 332 was discovered when a dumb kid planted a 332 seed in his family's suburban back yard in Orlando, FL. Then a castle grew and demolished a neighborhood. The whole town needed to be amnesticized, and the Foundation told the it was an amusement park, eventually opening the park for business to generate revenue (after ensuring the anomaly was safe and stable).

item.title: Wikiwalk Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
edit: edits made

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team.

+ Show proposed edits
- Hide

To link to another skip featuring castles, I propose the following edit:

On rare occasions, when a castle has formed, there is already a staff of servants within utterly dedicated to the original planter, although they are often inhuman in appearance.

to

On rare occasions, when a castle has formed, there is already a staff of servants within utterly dedicated to the original planter, although they are often inhuman in appearance.1

Footnotes
1. While no conclusive link between the two has been discovered, SCP-2448 is notably similar in that it is a castle that occasionally manifests humanoid denizens.

My theory on the inhuman appearanced servants is they are made exactly for whatever purpose they have. For example a floor cleaner might be sort of like a giant slug scraping up stuff on the floor of the castle and leaving a trail of nice-smelling slime behind whereas a fighter would look sort of like a suit of medieval armor as made by H. R. Giger and a butler would be sort of a skinny skeletal humanoid shape with far to many arms. The only things they would have in common would be lacking any reproductive system, rather they just grow out of the castle floor and utter obsessive loyalty to the castle owner in a weird stalkerish way.

All in all I really like this idea.
